connections.why: Atomic structure, bonding and the mole are extended to energetics, equilibria and group chemistry
Quantitative concepts like the mole are applied in titrations and practical work
Rates and equilibrium ideas are investigated experimentally
Bonding and shapes underpin the mechanisms of organic reactions
Thermodynamics and kinetics extend into deeper physical and organic chemistry
Organic functional groups are identified by the spectroscopic methods studied later
Redox and group chemistry lead into transition metals and electrochemical cells
Organic preparations and analysis are carried out in further practical work
Transition-metal and electrochemistry experiments draw on advanced practical skills
Foundational practical techniques are built on by the A2 practical assessment
